subtitle: The Master’s Cistern

briefing.text: Vael is dead. Destroy the remaining invasion and keep the cistern in estate hands.
The forward screen is broken. Destroy the remaining invasion, or hold a garrison at the cistern while the servants clear the intake. The culvert remains an approach for both sides.
Vael’s troops hold the estate cistern. Break their forward screen. The dry culvert opened in the previous battle reaches behind their thorned road position.

intro.text: Vael has crossed into the estate and choked the cistern intake. So much for his boundary.

dialogue.text: The grove is still untouched. Make him answer for what he does here. I will stand by our agreement.

alternative.text: The grove stays uncut. That was the agreement, and the culvert gives us all the approach we need.

intro.text: Our passage comes out behind their spears. Break the forward screen. Then we can turn the roots out of the intake.
You would have dug your road through our grove. I will close every approach before I let you try again.
Watch the passage behind us. Those fresh tracks are wolves, and they are not going toward the grove.
There is an isolated patrol on the northern road. Take its road fork or bring down its wolf outrider; either should break its hold on our flank.
He has brought a boar and a living tree into the basin. Keep our casters screened; their blows will break exposed bones.
Wolves have come around the crypt road behind us. Screen the keep while the levy breaks into the basin; we cannot fight this from our gate.

victory.text: Water through the intake, servants at the gate, and no roots on the road. My master has his cistern back.

debrief: The crypt and cistern remain the lich’s estate. The repaired intake and the opened culvert keep the waterworks reachable; the grove stands beyond the old boundary, uncut.
